In adults with heart failure, does empagliflozin compared with placebo reduce the first occurrence of adjudicated cardiovascular death or adjudicated hospitalisation for heart failure -- the outcome BOTH trials register as their primary?

External benchmark

No independent external benchmark exists. This pool is narrowed to a specific estimand: stable chronic heart failure, the registered primary composite of cardiovascular death or first hospitalisation for heart failure, time to first event. On that estimand EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved are the two large contributing trials, and the participant-level EMPEROR-Pooled analysis covers exactly this pair -- a same-trials cross-check, not an independent external benchmark. Empagliflozin has been studied in other heart-failure settings (EMPULSE, ~530, acute HF, hierarchical win-ratio outcome; EMPA-RESPONSE-AHF, ~80; EMPAG-HF), but those address different populations and endpoints, are not commensurable with the EMPEROR registered primary hazard ratios, and are not pooled here. A genuinely independent external benchmark on this specific estimand does not exist.

Heterogeneity

Q = 0.2785 on 1 df, I² 0%, τ² 0. Q = 0.2785 on 1 df, I-squared 0.0 per cent, tau-squared 0.0 under REML: the two trials agree closely. This pool combines the two trials' REGISTERED-PRIMARY HAZARD RATIOS for the two-component endpoint (cardiovascular death or first hospitalisation for heart failure, time to first event); it does NOT combine odds ratios. The earlier odds-ratio-over-unequal-follow-up concern was the reason that analysis was superseded on 2026-08-20 and does not apply to this hazard-ratio pool. The dominant uncertainty here is the small number of trials (k=2), not between-trial spread.

Absolute effect, at baseline risks you choose

Prefer Kaplan–Meier risks at a fixed time where the trials report them; the conversion below is the proportional-hazards approximation used only when they do not.

A HR of 0.77 implies, at a baseline risk B and at a stated time horizon: under proportional hazards the treated risk is 1−(1−B)HR, so ARR = B − [1−(1−B)HR] and NNT = 1/ARR. This review declares no reference baseline risk, so no specific ARR or NNT is asserted — the relationship is stated as a formula, not invented from an assumed baseline, and it is the conversion correct for a HR (not the risk-ratio form B×(1−effect)).

Declared data gaps (named absences, not silence)

These are extractions this review owes and does not yet contain. A regeneration renders what the object holds; it cannot invent data never extracted. A declared gap is an honest page — absence of assessment is not a negative assessment, and a blank here would read as a false 'nothing to report'.

  • All-cause mortality — The time-to-event HAZARD RATIO is NOT extracted (owed from the EMPEROR primary publications under the source hierarchy). What the registrations DO report, and this object holds, is all-cause mortality as an incidence rate per 100 patient-years across the two arms: 10.71 and 10.06 (EMPEROR-Reduced) and 6.67 and 6.6 (EMPEROR-Preserved). The 0.91 (0.80-1.05) previously shown here was the CARDIOVASCULAR-DEATH pool mislabelled as all-cause mortality and is WITHDRAWN. All-cause mortality is a distinct outcome from the cardiovascular-death component and must not borrow its value.
  • Harms — no harms outcome extracted. Owed for empagliflozin in heart failure: genital mycotic infections; urinary-tract infections and hypotension (notably in EMPEROR-Preserved). A blank here is a declared gap, NOT a finding that no harms occurred.
  • Funding — not extracted. The EMPEROR trials were funded by Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly (owed as an explicit funding statement).
  • References — not extracted. Owed: the two EMPEROR primary publications and the EMPEROR-Pooled participant-level analysis, as a citable reference list.
  • EMPEROR-Pooled ejection-fraction attenuation — not extracted. The participant-level EMPEROR-Pooled analysis reports attenuation of the benefit at higher ejection fraction; this effect-modification finding is owed.

Comparison with published syntheses

Two trials, one drug, one endpoint verified word for word against both registrations. A published participant-level synthesis of EXACTLY these two trials exists: EMPEROR-Pooled, a prospectively planned individual-patient-data analysis of EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved (~9,718 patients), with multiple indexed publications. Our k=2 pool of the two registered PRIMARY hazard ratios is a study-level reconstruction that agrees with it in direction and magnitude; it is a same-trials cross-check, not independent evidence. Analyses withheld at this k (declared refusals, not omissions)

  • GOSH (graphical exploration of heterogeneity) — not reported at k=2. explores model fit across the 2^k study subsets; below k≈10 there are too few subsets for the cloud to be informative.
  • Trial-sequential analysis (TSA) — not reported at k=2. the required information size and O'Brien-Fleming boundaries are unstable with a handful of trials; a pooled point at this k is not a monitoring boundary.
  • Meta-regression — not reported at k=2. Cochrane Handbook advises ≈10 studies per covariate; fitting a moderator at this k over-fits and is not reported.
  • Funnel plot / Egger's test (small-study effects) — not reported at k=2. both have negligible power below k≈10 (Handbook 13.3.5.4); a funnel with this many points cannot distinguish asymmetry from chance.
